did_you_know.text: Did you know? The chapter opens with a heading identifying the prophecy as a vision from Isaiah son of Amoz concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
Did you know? According to the vision, in the latter days the mountain of the LORD’s temple will be the center toward which all nations will stream.
Did you know? The nations will seek to learn the ways of the LORD, and the verse emphasizes: “For instruction will go out from Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.”

Did you know? The result of divine judgment and instruction will be peace among the nations: swords will be beaten into plowshares, spears into pruning hooks, and the nations will no longer train for war.
Did you know? After describing the vision of peace, Isaiah gives the house of Jacob a practical appeal: “Come, let us walk in the light of the LORD.”
Did you know? Isaiah describes the house of Jacob as having adopted foreign customs and influences, including divination and alliances with foreigners.
Did you know? The chapter presents the abundance of silver, gold, horses, and chariots as signs of great material power.
Did you know? Alongside wealth and power, Isaiah describes an abundance of idols, to the point that people bow down to the work of their own hands.
Did you know? “The day of the LORD Almighty” is described as a day when all human pride will be humbled, and the LORD alone will be exalted.
Did you know? The chapter ends with a call not to rely on human beings, whose breath is in their nostrils, because their status is limited and fleeting compared with the glory of the LORD.
